title: Engineering two-phase cooling for high-flux electronics: From nucleation dynamics to transport-limited CHF and physics-informed design
Electrochemical energy technologies: Current progress and future opportunities for sustainable energy transitions
abstract: Transitioning from fossil fuel–based systems to renewable energy is central to achieving global net-zero and sustainability goals. Yet, the large-scale deployment of renewable energy technologies—such as solar, wind, and biomass, requires not only clean power generation but also sustainable approaches to energy storage, conversion, and utilization. This review discusses the pivotal role of electrochemical conversion technologies in this transition, focusing on renewable electricity–driven processes for green hydrogen production, biomass upgrading to platform chemicals, and carbon dioxide reduction to value-added products under mild conditions. We emphasize how integrating these electrochemical systems within circular, carbon-neutral energy networks can bridge the gap between renewable generation and industrial-scale chemical production. Furthermore, we examine the existing barriers and emerging opportunities for the widespread adoption of these technologies. In addition, we provided a unique perspective on the socioeconomic prospects associated with these technologies for their incorporation and diffusion to revert the negative impacts of current energy technologies rather than limiting towards scientific aspects of these technologies alone covered by the conventional review articles. The article also explores the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) in accelerating catalyst discovery, automating reaction mechanism exploration, and optimizing device fabrication. Collectively, this work outlines a roadmap toward scalable, intelligent, and sustainable electrochemical technologies that can drive the global transition to a net-zero energy future.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven and prediction of green biohydrogen derived from microalgae biorefinery: A review
abstract: As the global energy transition progresses, sustainable biohydrogen production is essential to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and mitigating climate change. Microalgae-based biohydrogen production is a promising renewable source that can serve as an environmentally friendly alternative to conventional hydrogen production methods. However, the challenges of microalgae-based biohydrogen production remain in improving hydrogen yield and process efficiency. This review explores both traditional and innovative approaches to biohydrogen production from microalgae. It examines biophotolysis, dark fermentation, and the use of stress conditions (e.g., sulfur deprivation) to enhance hydrogen yields. Additionally, the role of genetic engineering and microbial co-cultivation in improving hydrogen production is discussed. Artificial intelligence (AI) applications are highlighted for their role in optimizing hydrogen production by adjusting key variables in real-time. The review outlines the significant advancements in genetic modification, metabolic engineering, and AI-driven optimization, demonstrating how these techniques could be used to enhance the biohydrogen output. AI models have demonstrated the ability to predict and optimize factors such as light intensity, temperature, and nutrient levels to maximize hydrogen yield. In addition, simulation techniques using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with Aspen Plus are utilized to assess the feasibility of large-scale biohydrogen production. AI-driven optimization and advanced biotechnological methods are crucial to overcoming current limitations and improving efficiency. Scaling up biohydrogen production will require continued innovation in reactor design, energy efficiency, and process automation. Further research is essential to fully realize the potential of microalgae as a viable source of renewable hydrogen.

title: Modeling study on biomass gasification for H2-rich syngas production based on machine learning: A comprehensive review
abstract: With the popularization of artificial intelligence, machine learning-based prediction of biomass gasification is necessary, because it can provide advance prediction and improvement direction for gasification engineering. In the article, the biomass gasification processes and the main chemical reactions were systematically reviewed. The main machine learning models used in the current research are multiple linear regression, polynomial regression models, SVR, DL, RF, GBR, XGBoost, AdaBoost, ANN, other neural network models. A detailed introduction and performance comparison among them was conducted. Besides, the feature importance analysis (Garson's algorithm, Pearson correlation analysis and SHAP) methods and the model evaluation indexes were described. This review paper discussed in detail how sample quality, model selection, anti-overfitting, and uncertainty affect the predictive performance of the model. In addition, the key factors affecting H2 production rate were analyzed and summarized. The results showed that, in terms of model selection, for small sample sizes, the boosted model was more suitable for less noisy or missing data situations, and the bagged model was more suitable for poorer quality samples. For the key factor analysis of hydrogen-rich products, steam to biomass ratio (S/B) and equivalence ratio (ER) were the most influential positive and negative correlations on H2 yield. The application of machine learning can analyze and draw some helpful conclusions for biomass efficient-gasification from the perspective of big data. But it requires researchers to increase uncertainty analysis to enhance the reliability and interpretability of experiments.

title: Machine learning-accelerated distributed optimisation methods for optimal power flow: A review
abstract: Modern power grids have become increasingly complex, with greater uncertainty due to the widespread integration of renewable energy resources potentially leading to higher operating costs. The optimal operation of these networks can be accomplished using optimal power flow (OPF), a fundamental optimisation tool for power networks with objectives including generation cost minimisation. Whilst the OPF problem itself is not new, quickly solving problems of a practical scale remains an active research area. Two approaches here are distributed optimisation and, more recently, machine learning (ML). Distributed optimisation improves scalability, avoids single points of failure, and enhances user privacy, whilst ML has the potential to provide solutions significantly faster than traditional optimisation methods. The goal of this review is to present approaches that overlap both areas, identifying complementary aspects as well as areas for further exploration. For example, one drawback of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), a distributed optimisation algorithm, is that it has slow convergence. Several reviewed papers have mitigated this by using ML to accelerate convergence through the prediction of consensus variable values, demonstrating improvements in terms of convergence time. Challenges remain, including the generalisation of results across different network topologies, something with the potential to be addressed with additional ML models such as graph neural networks (GNNs). Further areas to explore at the intersection of these two fields are identified, including augmented Lagrangian alternating direction inexact Newton (ALADIN) and overlapping Schwarz decomposition optimisation methods, as well as ML models such as GNNs and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs).

title: Advances in machine learning for the prediction of fuel cell membrane degradation
abstract: This paper focuses on the role of machine learning (ML) in predicting the fuel cell membrane durability and degradation. Durability of fuel cells is critical for their widespread commercial adoption. Herein, the advances in ML algorithms for predicting degradation are reviewed, with a concentration on recent studies in performance evaluation, fault diagnosis, degradation monitoring, and durability prediction. Recent advances in this field are presented, including ML and deep learning (DL) as artificial neural networks (ANNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), support vector machines (SVMs), genetic algorithms (GAs), principal component analysis (PCA), etc. are presented. These models have demonstrated high accuracy in predicting fuel cell performance and system reliability. They offer a high prediction accuracy range between 84.3 and 99.72 %. In addition, Furthermore, the aim of improving and advancing the selection of optimal materials for fuel cell membranes using ML methods has contributed to the development of more durable fuel cell membranes using various strategies to mitigate the effects of degradation, which are listed in this paper. It was concluded that accurate prediction of fuel cell membrane degradation remains a significant challenge due to complex interactions between material properties, chemical reactions, and operational conditions. Therefore, the paper emphasizes the importance of ML-based optimization models, real-time monitoring strategies, and hybrid modeling methods to enhance predictive capabilities. Future research efforts should focus on developing interpretable ML models, improving hybrid approaches, and expanding high quality datasets.

title: Advancing z-factor prediction in natural gas systems using machine learning: A review of methods, challenges, and role in the global energy transition
abstract: Accurate prediction of the gas compressibility factor (or z-factor) underpins metering, allocation, reconciliation, and process optimization across gas value chains. We synthesized 41 studies on machine learning (ML) z-factor predictions of natural gas (NG) mixtures spanning data realism (Standing-Katz charts, literature compilations, and field NG mixtures), sample sizes (102 to 105), and model families (GMDH, MLP, kernels, ensembles). Meta-analysis of the error distributions, stability (box-plots), and R2 trends shows a clear learning curve: larger datasets reduce median errors with diminishing returns beyond 104 to 105 data samples; compact regularized MLPs and GMDH are reliable in small-data regimes (<103); kernels and ensembles dominate at mid-scale (103 to 104); and regularized/deep MLPs prevail at scale (>104). Using a Niger Delta case study (0.5≤Ppr≤7.0; 1.1≤Tpr≤2.8), the TR-KRR achieved MAE = 0.00490 and RMSE = 0.00652, outperforming DAK75 (MAE = 0.00560) and far exceeding BB73. Two gaps persist: impurity corrections (such as CO2 and H2S) are rarely included; and single-phase z-factor dominates despite the field relevance of two-phase behaviour. We recommend standardized data splits and metrics with stability reporting, impurity-aware and two-phase modelling, open composition-rich benchmarks, and robustness/uncertainty evaluation versus AGA-8/GERG baselines. By delivering sub-percent errors across broader operating envelopes, ML-based z-factor prediction strengthens MRV, reduces reconciliation imbalances, and supports a lower-emissions gas value chain.

title: Leveraging machine learning for optimized microgrid management: Advances, applications, challenges, and future directions
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive review of recent advancements in integrating machine learning (ML) techniques into microgrid management systems, focusing on enhancing sustainability, reliability, and operational efficiency. The primary contribution of this work lies in categorizing and critically comparing various ML approaches including supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, and deep learning based on their performance, scalability, data requirements, and real-time applicability. A novel aspect of this study is the detailed evaluation of how ML algorithms address key microgrid challenges such as fault detection, load forecasting, energy optimization, and cybersecurity. Unlike previous reviews, this work includes comparative performance metrics (e.g., MAE, RMSE) and real-world case study analyses (e.g., Brooklyn and Austin microgrids), demonstrating how ML integration resulted in up to 20 % reduction in operational costs and 15–30 % improvement in efficiency and fault response time. The study also identifies key limitations in current systems including data quality, model interpretability, and regulatory barriers and recommends future research directions involving federated learning, edge computing, and generative AI. These findings support the development of resilient, scalable, and intelligent energy systems aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Machine learning methods for understanding coal pyrolysis
abstract: Pyrolysis is a critical step in the thermal conversion of coal. A deep understanding of its mechanisms is essential for accurately predicting product yield and promoting clean, efficient coal conversion. However, the development of technologies for precise product yield prediction has been limited due to the heterogeneity of coal structures and the complexity of pyrolysis processes. Machine learning (ML), with its unique ability to handle complex, multidimensional and nonlinear systems, has attracted growing interest in coal pyrolysis research. This article provides a systematic review of the latest advances in applying ML models to coal and biomass pyrolysis, emphasising their significant potential for data-driven product yield prediction. While the 'black box' nature of ML models enables high-precision modelling, limitations exist in explaining the mechanisms of pyrolysis pathways. Therefore, exploring ML-driven methods to uncover pyrolysis mechanisms is crucial to bridge the gap between predictive modelling and understanding the scientific basis of coal conversion. To address core issues in the current coal pyrolysis field, such as fragmented, multi-source, heterogeneous data, and insufficient cross-scale correlation analysis, we propose constructing a high-throughput pyrolysis characterization platform and innovating data association mining techniques to establish a robust, multidimensional database. This would enable the development of practical ML models suitable for laboratory and industrial settings, reducing the experimental workload and the costs of industrial trial and error.

title: Advancements in bioelectrochemical systems: Electrogens and methanogens behaviour, stress adaptation, and artificial intelligence-driven approaches for sustainable bioenergy
abstract: Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) and microbial electrolysis cells integrated anaerobic digestion (MECs-AD) are the emerging technologies of bioelectrochemical systems (BES) that enhance bioenergy production from bio(mass)waste. This review has been dedicated to the understanding of technical and biological aspects of microbes (i.e., electrogens and methanogens) in MFCs and MECs-AD. A key focus lies in elucidating the bioelectrochemistry of BES, complex microbial behavior, and strategies for microbial inoculation (such as pure strains, mixed consortium, genetic engineering, and bioaugmentation) as mono-cultures and co-cultures. Approaches for methanogen suppression in MFCs and electrogens enhancement in MECs-AD systems are addressed systematically. The synergy between electroactive bacteria, methanogenic archaea, and nanowires in electrogens of BES is discussed. The application of stress (e.g., salinity, temperature fluctuations, pH extremes, hydraulic/shear stress, electromagnetic fields, and chemical inhibitors) to stabilize functional microbes is also explored. The implementation of mixed stresses on BES is recommended to be beneficial in stabilizing microbial communities. Highlights the artificial intelligence (AI) driven strain design and machine learning (ML) advancements in BES. Neural networks and random forest algorithms can predict gene knockouts/insertions to maximize electron transfer. Therefore, further research is needed to implement genetically modified strains using AI and ML algorithms. The review's findings underscore the need for continued study at the intersection of microbial ecology, materials science, and computational modeling to unlock the full potential of BES systems.

title: Artificial intelligence in wind turbine fault diagnosis: A systematic knowledge mapping and trend analysis
abstract: Over the past decade, fault diagnosis technology in the wind energy sector has advanced rapidly, yet existing reviews exhibit methodological and data source fragmentation. This study employs bibliometrics and content analysis to systematically trace the conceptual evolution and technological trajectory of intelligent fault diagnosis for wind turbines. Based on 1736 fault diagnosis papers published in mainstream journals and conferences between 2016 and 2025, it quantitatively reveals trends in research themes, methodologies, and focal points. This study critically examines the strengths, limitations, and application boundaries of existing diagnostic frameworks, highlighting practical challenges such as data imbalance, insufficient open benchmarking, and obstacles to digital twin deployment. It also evaluates emerging trends in integrating foundational models with digital twins, noting their potential for enhancing component-level precision diagnostics. The proposed roadmap centers on deep learning and multimodal models, leveraging robust shared data, unified industry standards, and comprehensive security–privacy protection mechanisms. It emphasizes causal inference and lightweight edge deployment technologies. By tracing historical developments and evaluating existing diagnostic approaches, this study aims to accelerate data-driven practices in wind power operations and maintenance while establishing reliable intelligent fault diagnosis systems—critical for ensuring stable power generation from wind turbines.

title: Machine learning accelerated data generation, process modelling and system optimization for biomass conversion and valorization
abstract: Biomass incorporates carbon captured from the atmosphere and represents a renewable carbon resource for producing valuable bio-based products used in industrial processes, contributing to defossilization and decarbonization. However, the characteristics of biomass, including high oxygen and moisture content and a low heating value, present techno-economic challenges. A promising approach involves understanding and developing biomass's intrinsic structure to convert it into high-value products, such as bio-based functional materials, platform chemicals, and high-energy fuels. Nevertheless, these biomass valorization routes face challenges, including the lack of biomass property databases, complex process modeling, and multi-objective optimization, hindering scale-up from lab to industry. With the advancement of artificial intelligence, machine learning (ML) offers new opportunities. In this review, we first summarize the current status of biomass valorization technologies, and then review recent advances in ML-assisted biomass valorization, including (i) ML-assisted development of fundamental biomass databases, particularly structural and property data; (ii) ML-assisted process modelling, emphasizing hybrid approaches that integrate data-driven and mechanism-driven methods to accurately model various biomass valorization pathways; and (iii) ML-assisted multi-objective optimization for system-level improvements. Finally, we outline the remaining challenges and future research directions.

title: Artificial intelligence empowering geothermal energy development: A full-lifecycle review from exploration to operation
abstract: Geothermal energy (GE), driven by heat from the Earth's interior, is a renewable energy source characterized by abundant reserves, wide geographic distribution, and stable supply. It can continuously provide baseload electricity and supports both power generation and direct heating. Compared with intermittent renewables such as wind and solar, GE's inherent stability gives it strategic value in grid regulation and energy security. However, the global development of GE remains in its early stages, accounting for less than 0.5 % of total renewable energy capacity. Key limitations include high uncertainty in resource exploration, costly and technically demanding drilling, strong reservoir heterogeneity, long project cycles, and restricted economic feasibility.Artificial intelligence (AI)—particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL)—offers new opportunities to overcome these challenges. AI excels at processing large datasets, identifying complex patterns, and forecasting system behavior, making it applicable across the GE lifecycle—from resource assessment and drilling optimization to reservoir modeling, production forecasting, and plant operation. In particular, ML/DL shows significant potential in enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), where reservoir complexity and sparse data pose major barriers. In recent years, rapid advancements in algorithms and insights from other industries have accelerated the adoption of ML/DL in GE development. Nevertheless, issues such as limited model generalizability, insufficient data quality, and lack of interpretability remain persistent obstacles.This review systematically examines representative applications of AI across the GE lifecycle, identifies key breakthroughs and current bottlenecks, and outlines future research directions. It aims to provide both theoretical guidance and practical insights for intelligent geothermal development.

title: A comprehensive review of reinforcement learning-based voltage control in smart grids
abstract: Voltage control is a critical challenge in modern smart grids, especially with the increasing integration of distributed energy resources, electric vehicles, and variable renewables. Reinforcement learning (RL), as a data-driven and adaptive control paradigm, has gained significant traction for real-time voltage regulation. This review presents a comprehensive and systematic survey of RL-based voltage control strategies, covering value-based, policy-based, model-assisted, meta-learning, multi-agent, and hierarchical approaches, with a focus on studies published between 2017 and 2025. The novelty of this work lies in its unified evaluation framework, which benchmarks RL methods not only by their control accuracy and training efficiency, but also by their scalability, generalization, safety guarantees, and suitability for deployment in realistic grid environments. Unlike prior reviews that focus narrowly on control performance or algorithm categories, this work integrates recent advances such as physics-informed learning, risk-aware RL, and federated learning into a broader discussion of real-world applicability. The analysis shows that modern RL controllers can regulate voltage within 1–2 % of nominal values, scale to networks with over 100 buses, and adapt to disturbances using relatively few training episodes. Model-based and off-policy strategies improve sample efficiency, while multi-agent and hierarchical designs enable decentralized scalability. We also address practical considerations, including communication overhead, cyber-resilience, and control architecture integration, to bridge the gap between academic research and operational deployment.

title: An overview of reinforcement learning for power electronic converters: Topology derivation, parameter design, and control implementation
abstract: Power electronic converters, as core devices in modern smart grids, face three major technical challenges in topology derivation, parameter design, and control implementation. The discrepancy between traditional manual solutions and the demands for intelligent operation is increasingly evident, primarily manifested in topology optimization relying on trial and error, time-consuming parameter tuning, and a lack of adaptability in control strategies under complex operating conditions. Reinforcement learning (RL)–based artificial intelligence methods, with their strong self-adaptability, multi-objective cooperative optimization potential, and intelligent control capabilities for complex nonlinear systems, offer a new pathway to address these issues. However, there remains a lack of systematic literature reviews on the application of RL algorithms in power electronic converters, which poses significant challenges for related research. To address this gap, this paper classifies and organizes the mainstream RL algorithms applied in power electronic converters, summarizes their specific applications in topology derivation, parameter design, and control implementation, and finally provides an outlook on the prospects of RL in this field.

title: Artificial intelligence in heliostat control and optimization for CSP plants: A critical review
abstract: This review evaluates how artificial intelligence (AI) enhances heliostat control and optimization in concentrated solar power (CSP) systems, a critical need as global emissions reached 41.6 billion metric tons in 2024. The paper systematically evaluates AI and optimization techniques across four critical domains including heliostat field layout optimization, tracking accuracy enhancement, aiming and alignment optimization, and heat flux prediction and control. Results demonstrate significant performance improvements, with genetic algorithms increasing optical efficiency by 14.62 % in heliostat layouts. Notably, layout optimization techniques have successfully reduced the required number of heliostats from 864 to 541. Deep learning models reduce computation time from 600 s to 1 s (≈99.8 % reduction) and achieve 99.7 % recognition accuracy for heliostat detection. Neural network-based adaptive control systems reduce tracking errors to within 0.1 mrad, while StyleGAN architectures achieve 90 % flux prediction accuracy. The integration of machine learning with differentiable ray tracing delivers higher irradiance predictions using only 6000 rays versus traditional methods requiring 1,500,000 rays, achieving a lower L1 loss of 0.4 compared to 0.59. These technical advancements translate into substantial economic benefits, including a 3–4 % reduction in the levelized cost of electricity and annual operational savings of up to $30,000 per MW. Furthermore, the AI-optimized system can avoid approximately 57,624 tons of CO2 emissions annually, strengthening their environmental value. The review highlights challenges such as data quality limitations, computational complexity, and practical deployment barriers. Future work should focus on developing robust, scalable control approaches that enhance the economic viability and long-term sustainability of CSP technologies.

title: A comprehensive review of green hydrogen production via electrolysis and thermolysis, and the prediction of potential natural hydrogen (aka gold hydrogen) presence using machine learning
abstract: The global push toward net-zero carbon emissions has heightened interest in hydrogen as a clean energy carrier. This review explores the challenge of establishing sustainable hydrogen production pathways by focusing on two pivotal forms: green hydrogen, produced from renewable sources through water splitting, and gold hydrogen, a naturally occurring resource found in subsurface environments. For green hydrogen, production methods based on electrolysis and thermochemical water-splitting cycles are reviewed, with emphasis on catalyst-driven technological advances and solar-powered electrolysis and thermolysis. To evaluate the potential for solar-powered water splitting, a comparative analysis of 30 countries, selected for data reliability and diversity in solar resource availability, indicates that 60 % are well-positioned for green hydrogen deployment, whereas 40 % encounter substantial resource-related limitations. In these constrained regions, gold hydrogen emerges as a promising alternative. This review identifies the key geological factors influencing the potential for its presence and examines the application of machine learning (ML) techniques to predict its spatial distribution. The analysis reveals that specific machine learning models can successfully identify patterns within geological data, aiding in the preliminary strategic selection of sites for future gold hydrogen exploration. Among the 11 regression algorithms evaluated, the Decision Tree Regressor exhibited the best performance, indicating the presence of pronounced hierarchical structures. Similarly, the Gradient Boosting Regressor provided additional reliability through its ensemble-based approach. These algorithms provide preliminary predictions of potential gold hydrogen occurrences in resource-scarce regions, making this ML-based approach both novel and highly applicable to industrial and research contexts.

title: Artificial intelligence-based design optimization for wind turbines: A comprehensive review of its methodologies, applications, and challenges
abstract: Although use of wind energy has increased significantly in the recent years, the design optimization of wind turbines (WTs) remains hindered by challenges such as computational efficiency, multi-objective trade-offs, and system complexity. While the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) has offers innovative solutions for aerodynamic design, structural optimization, and control systems, a systematic synthesis on how AI paradigms address these cross-domain challenges in WT design optimization is lacking. To bridge this gap, this review provides a comprehensive survey of AI-based design optimization methodologies for WTs, categorizing into supervised learning-based methods, unsupervised learning-based methods, and reinforcement learning-based methods. These methods are systematically mapped to specific design optimization challenges across key WT subsystems, including blades, towers, and generators. Through a critical examination of 177 related publications, this review demonstrates AI's transformative impact on the design optimization methods for WTs, and identifies the critical challenges of the methods including data scarcity for novel designs, interpretability of black-box models, and integration of multi-physics constraints, etc. Finally, future work has been proposed to emphasize hybrid digital twin frameworks, federated learning for distributed optimization, and quantum-inspired algorithms for large-scale WT design optimization problems.

title: Reinforcement learning-based optimization framework for carbon emission reduction and circularity enhancement in buildings
abstract: The increasing demand to reduce carbon emissions and resource consumption in the construction sector has necessitated the integration of circular economy (CE) principles with climate change mitigation (CM) strategies. This study proposes a novel framework that integrates the CE and CM objectives by identifying optimal policies using reinforcement learning (RL), specifically Q-learning. The environmental impacts (EIs) were assessed across the entire building life cycle using a cradle-to-cradle (C2C) system boundary. The effectiveness of the framework was demonstrated through a case study involving three alternatives for exterior materials, three for window systems, and two for structural systems. By incorporating the actions related to the Rs framework—repair, replacement, reuse, and recycling—into the RL model, the study derives optimal maintenance and replacement strategies throughout the building life cycle. When compared with baseline scenarios—none (no repair actions) and 10_minor (repairs made every 10 years)—the RL-based policy reduces the global warming potential by up to 42.9 % and 23.1 %, with average reductions of 12.5 % and 5.7 %, respectively. It also decreases the total waste generation by 29.6 % and 15.5 %, respectively. This research promotes methodological approaches to sustainable building analysis by providing a data-driven framework that integrates RL with life cycle environmental assessment. It supports informed decision-making by identifying strategies that enhance durability and circularity while minimizing the environmental burden.

title: Liquid amine-based CO2 capture: A review of absorbent systems innovation, multi-scenario applications, and machine learning-assisted optimization
abstract: Liquid amine-based CO2 capture has the advantage of high absorbing capacity and rate, ideal reusability, and low cost, making it one of the most widely investigated and applied carbon capture technologies all over the world. In this review, the absorbent systems, as the fundament of liquid-amine based CO2 capture, were summarized and divided into three categories by their components, namely amine-water, ionic liquid-based, and water-lean/nonaqueous systems. Furthermore, application scenarios based on different absorbent systems as well as techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) were discussed. Based on the understanding of absorbent systems and application scenarios, studies of machine learning (ML)-assisted optimization in liquid amine-based CO2 capture were elucidated from molecular and process levels. To uncover the full potential of liquid amine-based CO2 capture technology, current challenges and further perspectives were proposed. This review aims to help researchers gain a deep understanding of liquid amine-based CO2 capture technology and further promoting more proper absorbent systems for practical usage.

title: Synergizing microbial and artificial intelligence technologies in food Systems: Innovations, safety, and sustainable pathways
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and microbial biotechnology are significantly advancing the redesign of food systems to make them sustainable, robust, and safe. This review presents a comprehensive discussion on the synergy between the different microbial innovations, such as precision fermentation, bio-preservation, and microbiome-informed functional foods, with AI tools throughout the supply chain from farm to fork. It identifies machine learning, computer vision, biosensors, and blockchain-based traceability as key components of Industry 4.0 and the emerging Food System 5.0 paradigms, and discusses their applications in real-time microbial detection, predictive risk evaluation, and supply chain optimization. Notably, the review places these technological advancements in the context of energy sustainability, climate change, and transitions, highlighting the potential applications of AI-microbial integration to energy intensity, efficient cold chain, waste-related embodied energy, and bioenergy/renewable-powered food systems. It also emphasizes the importance of an integrated ecosystem in which AI drives strain development, process control, smart packaging, and bioeconomy strategies such as food-waste valorization. Besides, the review brings in a critical perspective and raises the issues of antimicrobial resistance, data quality issues, digital divide, and regulatory and ethical uncertainties as limitations. In parallel, this review highlights gaps in life-cycle assessment and quantitative energy measures while critically addressing limits related to antibiotic resistance, data quality, digital infrastructure, and regulatory ambiguity. It demands comprehensive assessments that link advancements in food safety to measurable energy saving, carbon reduction, and integration of renewable energy.

title: From copper-chromite to MXenes: A century of furfural hydrogenation – Experiments, DFT, machine learning, and path forward
abstract: Furfural hydrogenation is a key step in converting biomass-derived platform molecules into value-added chemicals and fuels. This review covers experimental and computational work from 1929 to 2025, starting with early copper and nickel catalysts and moving to today's bimetallic alloys, MXene-supported systems, and Pt/aluminosilicates. We examine how metal composition, support acidity, solvent choice, and hydrogen pressure steer selectivity toward furfural alcohol (FA), 2-methylfuran (2-MF), tetrahydrofurfural alcohol (THFA), or the two pentanediols. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations, including our recent work, reveal adsorption geometries, activation barriers, and branching pathways, while machine-learning (ML) models predict high FA selectivity for optimized bimetallic systems. A unified scheme is proposed that integrates initial carbonyl hydrogenation, side-chain hydrogenolysis, full ring saturation, and ring-opening routes, whether from THFA or directly from FA (our patented catalysts and recent Pt/aluminosilicate results). Key factors controlling selectivity are discussed in detail. Catalyst deactivation, noble-metal cost, and scale-up remain hurdles; non-precious metals, robust supports, and combined theory-experiment loops offer practical fixes. Techno-economic viability is highlighted, with minimum selling prices (MSP) of ∼$1300 t−1 for FA (single-step) and higher for diols due to complexity, alongside lifecycle benefits (near-zero or net-negative CO2 with renewable H2 for FA production). The discussion concludes with concrete directions for selective, stable, and industrially viable furfural upgrading.

title: Leveraging machine learning for sustainable biochar and hydrochar production: Advances, challenges, and perspectives in thermochemical processes
authors: Sheikh Ahmad Faiz Sheikh Ahmad Tajuddin
abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) into thermochemical processes—including pyrolysis, hydrothermal carbonization (HTC), gasification, and torrefaction—for biochar and hydrochar production from diverse organic wastes (e.g., food and agricultural residues, seafood, and shellfish processing by-products) has significantly advanced the understanding and optimization of these conversion technologies. Unlike previous reviews that focused on isolated processes or provided general overviews of ML applications, the present review offers a unique cross-process comparative framework that links modeling strategies, feature selection, and algorithm performance across all major thermochemical routes. Building on this comprehensive perspective, the review further examines the applications of biochar and hydrochar in renewable energy systems. It also explores the role of ML in accurately predicting key properties, including yield, composition, and calorific value. By optimizing process parameters and minimizing the need for extensive experimental trials, ML provides a data-driven approach to enhance process understanding and performance. Among thermochemical conversion methods, pyrolysis has been the most extensively investigated, and ensemble learning algorithms such as random forest regression and gradient boosting regression have demonstrated superior predictive accuracy. ML has also proven effective in modeling hydrochar characteristics in HTC, reinforcing its relevance to sustainable system development. However, the limited number of ML-based investigations on gasification and torrefaction constrains a more detailed comparative assessment, presenting opportunities for future research. This review highlights the importance of feature selection and dataset quality in ML modeling and emphasizes integrating ML into techno-economic and environmental assessments. Despite challenges in data availability and model generalization, advancements in sensor technologies and hybrid modeling approaches offer promise for real-time process monitoring. Overall, ML has strong potential to develop efficient, scalable, and sustainable biochar and hydrochar systems.

title: Applications of artificial intelligence for PVT heat pump systems: A review
abstract: In building heating and cooling field, photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) integrated with heat pump systems have become more and more attractive owing to their strengths of high energy efficiency and sustainability. However, the structure of PVT heat pump systems is complicated and it appears nonlinearity and dynamic characteristics in the operation process, thus posing significant challenges for control. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) has garnered increasing attention as transformative tools for addressing these issues. On the basis of retrospecting and summarizing the novel PVT heat pump systems, the paper delves into a detailed analysis of AI applications in PVT heat pump systems, concentrating on four key areas: modeling, prediction, control and fault detection and diagnosis. The review outlines various AI approaches, including machine learning and deep reinforcement learning, and discusses their strengths and limitations when applied in PVT heat pump systems. Furthermore, the paper identifies key research deficiencies and promising pathways for the application of AI in this field.

title: Advances in artificial intelligence-enabled fault detection for virtual power plants
abstract: With the accelerating integration of renewable energy sources, virtual power plants (VPPs) have emerged as a key paradigm for aggregating and managing distributed energy resources. However, the inherent complexity, heterogeneity, and dynamic behavior of VPPs make them highly susceptible to faults, which can undermine system reliability, operational efficiency, and grid stability. Although previous research has examined specific aspects of fault diagnosis in VPPs, such as cyber threats and faults in individual resources, there is still a lack of comprehensive reviews that systematically address fault types and diagnostic methodologies across the entire VPP architecture. To address this gap, a structured and multi layered review of VPP fault diagnosis is presented. The VPP architecture is divided into three functional layers, namely aggregation, communication, and market interface, and the main fault types, cross layer interactions, and their potential impacts are analyzed in detail. In addition, a task oriented functional taxonomy of six representative artificial intelligence approaches, including feedforward neural networks, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, graph neural networks, federated learning, and reinforcement learning, is established. These methods are systematically reorganized and comparatively analyzed according to their roles, capabilities, and applicability across different VPP operational layers. Finally, the major challenges of deploying AI-driven methods in VPPs are identified, and future research directions are proposed to enhance the adaptability, scalability, and resilience of VPP systems, thereby supporting the reliable and sustainable operation of renewable energy-dominated grids.

title: Integrated assessment of energy systems: opportunities and barriers for digital twin and artificial intelligence adoption
abstract: Digital twins and artificial intelligence offer transformative capabilities for energy system assessment and present meaningful insights into the complex interplay between thermodynamic performance, economic viability, and environmental sustainability. In this Review, we examine the trends, major frameworks, assessment dimensions, and key barriers shaping integrated energy system evaluation. Roughly 12.7% of studies in the current literature integrate all four assessment dimensions-thermodynamic analysis, techno-economic assessment, life cycle assessment, and digital twin or AI integration-rather than addressing them in isolation. As such, single-dimension assessment dominates the field, with thermodynamic modelling, techno-economic assessment, and life cycle assessment each addressed independently in 67.6%, 53.9%, and 47.1% of reviewed studies respectively, while only 31.4% incorporate digital twin or AI components. These disciplinary silos are also driving assessment inconsistency, with methodological choices alone generating cost variation of up to 133% for physically identical production systems. However, the integrated frameworks that do exist have remained consistently superior in decision-making quality, with the 13 fully integrated studies producing qualitatively different technology rankings and cost-parity thresholds compared to single-dimension analyses. Integrated assessment can mitigate the risk of misallocated investment and policy error, although there are concerns about the disconnect between operational optimisation and lifecycle consequences, and the absence of standardised cross-dimensional costing protocols. Indeed, approximately 87.3% of economic studies ignore exergy destruction costs and 95.8% of life cycle assessments rely on static rather than dynamic inventories. Future integrated assessment frameworks must account for factors such as real-time dynamic life cycle inventory updating, standardised exergoeconomic costing, equity dimensions, and empirical validation of multi-year predictions.

title: Artificial intelligence for geological CO2 storage: From surrogate prediction to uncertainty-aware decision making
abstract: Geological CO2 storage (GCS) is a key technology for achieving net-zero emissions; however, its gigatonne-scale deployment remains constrained by the difficulty of accurately predicting subsurface CO2 migration and rigorously quantifying associated uncertainty and risk. Although physics-based numerical simulators provide high-fidelity representations of coupled multiphase flow processes, their substantial computational cost severely limits ensemble-based uncertainty quantification (UQ) and decision-oriented analyses. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled a new generation of surrogate modeling frameworks that are transforming GCS from simulation-based prediction to risk-informed lifecycle management. This review provides a critical synthesis of this evolution, proposing a unified framework that bridges algorithmic advances with engineering decision-making. We trace the evolution of AI surrogates in GCS, from classical statistical surrogates and grid-dependent deep learning models to physics-informed frameworks and resolution-invariant neural operators, critically assessing their strengths and limitations for long-horizon subsurface CO2 plume migration forecasting. Furthermore, our analysis of AI-driven UQ in GCS focuses on generative geological modeling for characterizing aleatoric uncertainty and Bayesian frameworks for quantifying epistemic uncertainty, with particular emphasis on their limitations and scalability. Crucially, we extend this analysis to closed-loop decision frameworks and highlight that the main challenge in field-scale deployment lies in bridging the simulation-to-reality gap. This requires continuous data assimilation and uncertainty-aware digital rehearsal. Finally, we identify key challenges and provide a strategic roadmap toward next-generation intelligent GCS ecosystems. Central to this roadmap is an integrated lifecycle framework linking prediction, UQ, and operational decision-making, providing a pathway toward scalable, trustworthy, and adaptive GCS management.

title: Advances in machine learning for biomass pyrolysis: Product prediction, process optimization and mechanistic interpretation
abstract: Biomass pyrolysis has attracted significant attention because of its ability to simultaneously produce fuels and value-added chemicals. However, both conventional and advanced pyrolysis methods still exhibit limited predictive accuracy and applicability. In addition, biomass pyrolysis involves complex reaction pathways, and product distributions are influenced by multiple factors, including feedstock properties, reaction conditions, and catalysts. With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for biomass pyrolysis research. By establishing non-linear relationships between inputs and outputs, ML has demonstrated strong potential for product prediction, process optimization, and reaction mechanism interpretation. This review summarizes recent progress in the application of ML for predicting multiple pyrolysis products, including biochar, bio-oil and syngas. It also discusses the integration of optimization algorithms, such as genetic algorithms (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and bayesian optimization algorithms (BOA), for process optimization and inverse design. Furthermore, the integrated application of ML with explainable AI (XAI), physical constrained models, and advanced representation techniques has shown unique advantage in elucidating reaction mechanisms and characterizing feedstock structures. In addition, this review highlights the potential of ML in sustainability assessment through its integration with life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA). Finally, key challenges and future research directions are discussed to support the development of reliable, efficient, and sustainable ML-assisted biomass pyrolysis systems.

title: Machine learning-assisted design and optimization of thermoacoustic devices: Progress and perspectives
abstract: Thermoacoustic technology plays an important role in the development of renewable energy. Owing to its simple structure, reliable operation, and environmental friendliness, it has been widely applied in energy-related fields such as refrigeration, power generation, and waste heat recovery. However, the performance of thermoacoustic systems highly depends on the coordinated matching among multiple components, and the design and optimization process is characterized by strong nonlinearity and multi-parameter coupling, making traditional methods inefficient. With the development of artificial intelligence (AI), data-driven modeling and global optimization capabilities have gradually promoted research progress in performance improvement and parameter optimization of thermoacoustic devices. Therefore, this paper focuses on thermoacoustic engines (TAEs), thermoacoustic refrigerators (TARs), and their key components, and systematically reviews the current applications and future prospects of machine learning in performance prediction, parameter optimization, and design optimization. This paper aims to help readers comprehensively understand the development trends of machine learning-assisted thermoacoustic research and provide references for its engineering applications and technological innovation in the field of green energy utilization.

title: Towards smart thermal energy management: A review on machine learning for control and optimization of active phase change systems in buildings
abstract: The building sector constitutes a substantial share of global energy consumption and carbon emissions, highlighting the critical need for the development of near-zero energy buildings and smart energy systems. Active phase change material (PCM) systems incorporate dynamic components to facilitate on-demand control of PCM energy storage and release processes, significantly improving the thermal management capabilities and energy scheduling flexibility of building envelopes. However, these systems exhibit complex characteristics, including multivariable interactions, strong nonlinearity, and time-varying behaviors. These complexities pose significant challenges for traditional physics-based modeling and rule-based control methods in achieving real-time optimization and global decision-making. Consequently, such methods often encounter issues like high computational costs, limited accuracy, and inadequate adaptability. Recently, the advent of machine learning technologies has introduced a novel, data-driven paradigm to address these challenges. This review systematically examines research on machine learning applications for controlling and optimizing active PCM systems in buildings. Initially, it explores research advancements and key design parameters for active PCM systems integrated into walls, floors, and ceilings. Subsequently, it critically evaluates the limitations of traditional methods while detailing the opportunities and breakthrough applications enabled by machine learning, including efficient alternate modeling, intelligent control, and multi-objective parameter optimization. Finally, it provides a comprehensive discussion of current research, highlights major challenges such as data dependence, model interpretability, and real-time deployment, and outlines future research directions. The aim of this work is to promote the deep integration of machine learning, building physics, and energy systems engineering, offering valuable insights for the development of next-generation intelligent, adaptive, and low-carbon building energy systems.

title: Data driven reveals the upgrading mechanism of waste PET electrolysis: Research progress of machine learning in collaborative production of high-value chemicals and green hydrogen energy
abstract: The pollution of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics poses a global environmental challenge, and traditional recycling technologies are limited by downgrading cycles and high energy consumption. Electrocatalytic upgrading recycling can convert waste PET into high-value chemicals and synergistically produce hydrogen under mild conditions, but its multi-step electron/proton transfer, competitive reaction pathway, and complex catalyst structure-activity relationship make it difficult to efficiently break through traditional trial and error methods. Machine learning (ML), as a data-driven new paradigm, provides systematic solutions for rational catalyst design, deep mechanism analysis, and multi-objective system optimization by integrating multi-source data, constructing quantitative structure-activity relationships, analyzing reaction networks, and intelligently navigating parameter spaces. This review is the first to construct a full chain methodological framework of data algorithm application, systematically reviewing the latest progress of ML in the field of PET electrolysis collaborative production of high-value chemicals and green hydrogen energy, and looking forward to cutting-edge directions such as independent experiments, generative AI, and multimodal fusion, aiming to provide theoretical guidance for the technological development and knowledge system construction in this field.

title: From classical to AI-driven load frequency control: Addressing smart grid challenges with renewable energy sources and EVs integration
abstract: This research investigates advancements in Load Frequency Control (LFC) by examining AI-based and optimization-driven strategies aimed at improving frequency stability in Multi-Area Power Systems (MAPSs). The study offers a broad evaluation, transitioning from early classical approaches to emerging modern and AI-driven techniques. A key methodological contribution is the structured comparison of traditional, intelligent, and optimization-based controllers evaluated by using standardized performance indices such as ITSE under realistic system conditions, including nonlinearities (GRC, GDB, CTD) and communication delays. It assesses various control strategies, emphasizing the adaptability and robustness required for effective LFC in dynamic environments. Particular attention is also paid to optimization methods and artificial controllers. The study also evaluates the impacts of energy storage technologies, electric vehicles (EV), and renewable energy sources on the system frequency stability. Moreover, it also investigates machine learning and reinforcement learning frameworks with the potential to address LFC issues. The paper contains critical smart grid issues like potential cybersecurity threats, controller failures, data transmission errors and communication boundaries. It also introduces a systematic Scopus-based literature filtration process, resulting in a publication trend analysis that reveals evolving research directions. Providing practical insights and novel approaches, this work aims to divert future studies toward more stable, flexible, and robustness-based LFC solutions in a more practical complex power system realization.

title: Transformer-based renewable energy forecasting: A comprehensive review
abstract: Accurate renewable energy forecasting (REF) is critical for efficient power system planning, management, and operation, given the intermittent and stochastic nature of renewable energy sources (RESs). Transformer-based models have emerged as a promising solution for REF due to their superior ability to model sequential dependencies and capture complex spatiotemporal patterns. This paper presents a comprehensive and methodologically structured review of Transformer-based approaches for renewable energy forecasting, analyzing their unique advantages, inherent challenges, and practical deployment considerations. We systematically examine key Transformer variants and their applications across solar, wind, and other RESs, while establishing a generalized REF framework. A quantitative comparison with conventional deep learning techniques demonstrates that Transformer models achieve a significant improvement in forecasting accuracy. Additionally, we explore recent advancements in Transformer architectures, data preprocessing methods, and optimization strategies that further enhance their predictive performance and computational efficiency. By synthesizing current research trends, this review offers actionable insights for practitioners and identifies future directions to advance scalable and reliable Transformer-based forecasting systems. Our findings underscore the transformative potential of Transformer models in elevating the accuracy and robustness of REF, providing a valuable reference for researchers and industry stakeholders.

title: AI-enabled fault diagnosis for hydrogen fuel cells: recent advances, challenges, and future perspectives
abstract: Ensuring the operational reliability and safety of hydrogen fuel cells has become a critical research focus. The inherently coupled multi-physics nature of fuel cells gives rise to diverse and nonlinear fault mechanisms, presenting substantial challenges for conventional model-based diagnostic approaches. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a compelling alternative, owing to its strong capabilities in data-driven pattern recognition and adaptive learning. In this study, typical faults and diagnosis execution process in fuel cell systems were systematically reviewed. At the core, unlike existing reviews that primarily classify methods by algorithmic categories or application scenarios, we systematically evaluate the applicability and limitations of representative AI techniques at each diagnostic stage from data acquisition to control adaptation. Finally, the key challenges that hinder real-world deployment are discussed, and emerging research trends are prospected. This review's contribution lies in offering a new perspective by connecting diagnostic workflow requirements with AI capabilities, which reframes how researchers should match techniques to fuel cell system challenges.

title: Toward greener shipping: A systematic review of AI-driven solutions for environmental performance in maritime operations
abstract: Decarbonizing maritime transport is a central challenge for global climate policy, as the sector combines high greenhouse gas intensity with complex operational and regulatory constraints. Compliance with evolving International Maritime Organization (IMO) instruments, including the Carbon Intensity Indicator and the IMO Net-Zero Framework, requires decision-support tools capable of operating under heterogeneous data environments and operational uncertainty. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as data-driven emission-reduction strategies in maritime operations. This systematic review examines how AI/ML models are designed, validated, and applied to improve environmental performance and regulatory alignment in the maritime sector. Using a PRISMA-based methodology, peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2025 are analyzed and classified across core application domains, including predictive maintenance, performance and emissions prediction, route and speed optimization, surveillance and navigation, and design and manufacturing. The review distinguishes between base models, which emphasize predictive accuracy under controlled conditions, and robustness-oriented models, which address cross-vessel generalization, validation under variable operational scenarios, sensitivity to data uncertainty, and fleet-level transferability. The synthesis shows that while many base models achieve high predictive performance, robustness remains limited due to fragmented data standards, scarce real-world validation, and weak integration with regulatory systems. Based on these findings, three policy implications are derived: (i) standardized digital emissions and performance data formats are required to enable scalable AI deployment; (ii) AI- monitoring should be formally recognized within IMO compliance and reporting mechanisms; and (iii) regulatory incentives should prioritize robust, fleet-level AI solutions over vessel-specific pilots.

title: Energy harvesting in hybrid electric vehicles and railway systems: AI-enabled condition monitoring and emerging trends
abstract: Modern electric and hybrid transportation platforms employ numerous sensors, controllers, and communication modules that require continuous power supply. Energy harvesting technologies offer a promising solution to support these auxiliary systems and reduce dependency on the primary battery. This article systematically evaluates major energy harvesting technologies such as Thermoelectric generators (TEGs), Regenerative Braking systems (RBS), Regenerative shock absorbers (RSAs) and other vibration harvesting technologies, as the potential solution to provide the power supply in the onboard auxiliaries and self-sensing modules. A comparative analysis is presented in terms of working principles, energy conversion potential, operational characteristics, and practical implementation in transportation systems. TEGs exploit exhaust-gas thermal gradients, RBS recovers kinetic energy typically discarded as heat and RSAs transform vibrations caused by suspensions to electrical energy without affecting ride comfort. To further the discussion, the review also applies the same to railway applications where bogie, axle-box and track-mounted harvesters enabled self-powered monitoring and predictive maintenance. Adaptive power distribution, autonomous health management, and self-sustaining IoT-based transport (IoTT) further are backed up by the integration of mechanical intelligence and AI-enabled energy management. In general, this review demonstrates the prospect of multi-source hybrid harvesters to eliminate traction battery dependence and to extend the vehicle range and facilitate a fully self-powered cyber-physical transportation platform.
